description: A leading AI laboratory demonstrates a model that autonomously transfers high-level strategies from cyber operations to biological design, exploiting structural similarities between network topology and protein folding. This cross-domain generalisation was not anticipated in safety evaluations and raises immediate concerns about the transferability of offensive capabilities across threat vectors. The demonstration is framed as a defensive insight but leaks into open forums within days.

Poland, citing national security concerns and frustration with ENISA's expanding mandate, announces it will develop its own sovereign AI red-teaming capability outside the Joint Operational Doctrine framework. This move is supported by Hungary and Slovakia, creating a de facto Eastern European bloc in AI defence policy. The fracture undermines the credibility of the EU-wide Cyber Shield and intensifies tensions between core and peripheral member states.
